questions.text: What year of study is Aliya Serikova in at WKU?
questions.hint: "I study Medicine at WKU — it is my THIRD YEAR, and graduation is only two years away." — Aliya.

questions.text: Aliya's internship is going to include three different medical departments.
questions.hint: "I am going to work in THREE DIFFERENT DEPARTMENTS: general medicine, paediatrics, and emergency care." — Aliya describes her upcoming internship.

questions.text: Where is Aliya going to work after her one-year internship?
opts: At a private clinic in Astana
At the Regional Hospital in Taraz
questions.correct: At the Regional Hospital in Taraz
questions.hint: "After the internship, I am going to move back to my hometown of Taraz... to work at the Regional Hospital there." — her clear plan.

questions.text: Aliya is going to apply for a Master's degree in ___ Health in three or four years.
questions.hint: "I am going to apply for a Master's degree in PUBLIC Health." — Aliya wants to study health systems and improve healthcare for communities.

questions.text: Kairat is going to spend the whole summer with his family in Semey.
questions.hint: "I am going to spend TWO WEEKS in Semey with my family." — Not the whole summer. First he's doing a six-week internship in Astana.

questions.text: What is the name of the tech company where Kairat is going to do his internship?
questions.hint: "I am going to do an internship at a tech company in Astana. The company is called DATABRIDGE SOLUTIONS — they build data analysis tools for businesses."

questions.text: The whole family is going to visit ___ together in August — Kairat's grandmother has always wanted to go.
questions.hint: "In August, the whole family is going to travel to TURKESTAN — all seven of us... My grandmother has always wanted to see the Yasawi Mausoleum."

questions.text: What are Kairat's two plans for next year at WKU?
opts: Transfer to Almaty university and find a job
Apply for a scholarship and join the Computer Science Club
Take a year off and travel around Kazakhstan
Move to a different dormitory and change his major
questions.correct: Apply for a scholarship and join the Computer Science Club
questions.hint: "I am going to apply for the WKU Academic Excellence Scholarship... Second, I am going to join the Computer Science Club." — two clear goals.

questions.text: What is Aibek going to do immediately after exams finish?
opts: Sleep for twelve hours, then pack and go to Aktau
questions.correct: Sleep for twelve hours, then pack and go to Aktau
questions.hint: "FIRST I'M GOING TO SLEEP FOR ABOUT TWELVE HOURS! Then I'm going to pack and go home to Aktau." — Aibek's immediate post-exam plan.

questions.text: Gulim is going to visit a famous architecture firm in Astana.
questions.hint: "I'm going to visit a famous architecture firm — in ALMATY." — NOT Astana. The firm that offered Gulim a tour is in Almaty.

questions.text: Gulim's mother is going to teach her to make her special ___ recipe.
questions.hint: "My mum is going to teach me her special BESHBARMAK recipe!" — Gulim describes her plans for the last two weeks of summer in Shymkent.

questions.text: How much is the hostel going to cost per night for Nurgul and Marat?
questions.hint: "I found a great hostel near the city centre — it's going to cost about 4,500 TENGE PER NIGHT EACH." — Marat reports the price to Nurgul.

questions.text: On Sunday, Nurgul and Marat are going to take a bus up to Shymbulak.
questions.hint: "On Sunday, we're going to take a CABLE CAR up to Shymbulak!" — NOT a bus. A cable car goes up the mountain from Medeu to the resort.

questions.text: What task does Nurgul take responsibility for in their planning?
opts: Booking the cable car online that evening
questions.correct: Booking the cable car online that evening
questions.hint: "I'm going to book the CABLE CAR online this evening." — Nurgul takes this task while Marat is going to book the train tickets.

questions.text: Aliya already has a plan. Complete the sentence: "Aliya ___ do a one-year internship."
questions.hint: Aliya = she = 3rd person singular → IS going to. "Aliya IS going TO do an internship." ✅ Pre-made plan + singular subject → IS going to.

questions.text: "She going to move to Taraz after graduation" is correct English.
questions.hint: FALSE! The "be" verb is missing! ✅ "She IS going to move to Taraz." The formula is: am/IS/are + going to + base verb. "She going to" has no "is" — always needed!

questions.text: Someone's phone rings during a lecture. Their friend says: "Don't worry, ___!"
questions.hint: Spontaneous decision made RIGHT NOW → WILL. "I'LL answer it!" ✅ The friend didn't plan this before the phone rang — they decided in that exact moment. Classic WILL situation.

questions.text: "Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain very soon!"
questions.hint: Evidence-based prediction (you can SEE the dark clouds) → IS going to. "It IS GOING TO rain!" ✅ The visible evidence (dark clouds) tells you rain is coming — this is going to, not will.

questions.text: Gulim asks Aibek about his summer. She says: "What ___ you ___ do this summer?"
questions.hint: "What ARE you GOING TO do this summer?" ✅ Wh- question formula: What + ARE (2nd person) + you + going to + do? Asking about pre-made plans → going to.

questions.text: "Won't" is the correct contraction of "will not".
questions.hint: TRUE! will not → WON'T ✅ It's an irregular contraction. "I won't forget." · "She won't be late." · "They won't come." — always WON'T, not "willn't".

questions.text: Marat bought the train tickets last week. "We ___ (leave) on Friday the 4th of October."
questions.hint: Tickets already bought = plan made BEFORE this conversation → GOING TO. "We ARE GOING TO leave on Friday." ✅ Pre-planned + "we" = ARE going to.

questions.text: Aliya thinks about the future of medicine in Kazakhstan. She says: "___ be more doctors here in the future."
questions.hint: "There WILL be more doctors here." ✅ General opinion/prediction about the future without specific evidence → WILL. "I think + will" is a common pattern for general predictions.

questions.text: What does "internship" mean?
opts: A final exam at the end of a university course
A period of work experience at a company, often for students
A type of scholarship for excellent students
A letter of recommendation from a professor
questions.correct: A period of work experience at a company, often for students
questions.hint: INTERNSHIP = стажировка. "I am going to do a one-year INTERNSHIP at the hospital." — practical work experience at an organisation, often unpaid or low-paid.

questions.text: "Permanent" means temporary and lasting only for a short time.
questions.hint: FALSE! PERMANENT = lasting forever or for a very long time; NOT temporary. "I'm not going to leave Kazakhstan PERMANENTLY." — Aliya means she will never leave for good. The opposite of permanent is temporary.

questions.text: "You must submit your application before the 15th of October — that is the ___."
questions.hint: DEADLINE = крайний срок. "The scholarship application DEADLINE is the 15th of October." — the latest date by which something must be done. After the deadline, it's too late!

questions.text: What does "achieve" mean?
opts: To make a plan for the future
To fail at something after trying hard
To successfully reach a goal after effort
To ask someone for help with a difficult task
questions.correct: To successfully reach a goal after effort
questions.hint: "I will look back and feel proud of what I have ACHIEVED." ACHIEVE = достигать. You work hard and successfully reach your goal — that is achievement.

questions.text: What does "consistent" mean?
opts: Doing something only once and then stopping
Changing your approach every day depending on mood
Doing the same thing reliably over time without stopping
Working only when someone tells you to
questions.correct: Doing the same thing reliably over time without stopping
questions.hint: "I won't follow this plan perfectly, but I will follow it CONSISTENTLY." CONSISTENT = последовательный. Study every day — not perfectly but without stopping. That is consistent effort.

questions.text: To "commit to a plan" means to decide you are probably going to stop following it.
questions.hint: FALSE! COMMIT to a plan = обязываться / давать обещание. It means you promise FIRMLY to follow through — the OPPOSITE of stopping. "I'm COMMITTED to this plan — I'm going to follow it." Full dedication.

questions.text: "4,500 tenge per night for a hostel — that's very ___ for travellers on a budget!"
questions.hint: AFFORDABLE = доступный по цене. "That's very AFFORDABLE!" — 4,500 tenge is cheap enough that most people can pay for it. Not too expensive. The opposite of expensive.

questions.text: What does "priority" mean in "My top priority this year is my academic work"?
opts: Something you do when you have free time and feel like it
Something that is more important than other things and must be done first
A type of reward you give yourself after finishing a project
A difficulty or obstacle that stands in your way
questions.correct: Something that is more important than other things and must be done first
questions.hint: "English and my academic work are my top PRIORITIES for this year." PRIORITY = приоритет. Your priority is the most important thing — it comes FIRST before everything else.
